class.name: OcgGeom2dBeziercurve
class.brief_description: Describes a rational or non-rational Bezier curve - a non-rational Bezier curve is defined by a table of poles (also called control points), - a rational Bezier curve is defined by a table of poles with varying weights. These data are manipulated by two parallel arrays: - the poles table, which is an array of gp_Pnt2d points, and - the weights table, which is an array of reals. The bounds of these arrays are 1 and "the number of poles" of the curve. The poles of the curve are "control points" used to deform the curve. The first pole is the start point of the curve, and the last pole is the end point of the curve. The segment which joins the first pole to the second pole is the tangent to the curve at its start point, and the segment which joins the last pole to the second-from-last pole is the tangent to the curve at its end point. It is more difficult to give a geometric signification to the weights but they are useful for providing exact representations of the arcs of a circle or ellipse. Moreover, if the weights of all the poles are equal, the curve is polynomial; it is therefore a non-rational curve. The non-rational curve is a special and frequently used case. The weights are defined and used only in case of a rational curve. The degree of a Bezier curve is equal to the number of poles, minus 1. It must be greater than or equal to 1. However, the degree of a Geom2d_BezierCurve curve is limited to a value (25) which is defined and controlled by the system. This value is returned by the function MaxDegree. The parameter range for a Bezier curve is [ 0, 1 ]. If the first and last control points of the Bezier curve are the same point then the curve is closed. For example, to create a closed Bezier curve with four control points, you have to give a set of control points P1, P2, P3 and P1. The continuity of a Bezier curve is infinite. It is not possible to build a Bezier curve with negative weights. We consider that a weight value is zero if it is less than or equal to gp::Resolution(). We also consider that two weight values W1 and W2 are equal if: |W2 - W1| <= gp::Resolution(). Warning - When considering the continuity of a closed Bezier curve at the junction point, remember that a curve of this type is never periodic. This means that the derivatives for the parameter u = 0 have no reason to be the same as the derivatives for the parameter u = 1 even if the curve is closed. - The length of a Bezier curve can be null.

method.name: from_NCollection_Array1_of_gp_Pnt2d_const_ref
method.description: Creates a non rational Bezier curve with a set of poles : CurvePoles. The weights are defaulted to all being 1. Raises ConstructionError if the number of poles is greater than MaxDegree + 1 or lower than 2.

method.name: from_Geom2d_BezierCurve_const_ref
method.description: Copy constructor for optimized copying without validation.

method.name: from_NCollection_Array1_of_gp_Pnt2d_const_ref_NCollection_Array1_of_double_const_ref
method.description: Creates a rational Bezier curve with the set of poles CurvePoles and the set of weights PoleWeights. If all the weights are identical the curve is considered as non rational. Raises ConstructionError if the number of poles is greater than MaxDegree + 1 or lower than 2 or CurvePoles and CurveWeights have not the same length or one weight value is lower or equal to Resolution from package gp.

method.name: ClearEvalRepresentation
method.description: Removes the evaluation representation.

method.name: Increase
method.description: Increases the degree of a bezier curve. Degree is the new degree of <me>. raises ConstructionError if Degree is greater than MaxDegree or lower than 2 or lower than the initial degree of <me>.

method.name: InsertPoleAfter
method.description: Inserts a pole with its weight in the set of poles after the pole of range Index. If the curve was non rational it can become rational if all the weights are not identical. Raised if Index is not in the range [0, NbPoles]

method.name: InsertPoleBefore
method.description: Inserts a pole with its weight in the set of poles after the pole of range Index. If the curve was non rational it can become rational if all the weights are not identical. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles+1]

method.name: RemovePole
method.description: Removes the pole of range Index. If the curve was rational it can become non rational. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles]

method.name: Reverse
method.description: Reverses the direction of parametrization of <me> Value (NewU) = Value (1 - OldU)

method.name: ReversedParameter
method.description: Returns the parameter on the reversed curve for the point of parameter U on <me>.

method.name: Segment
method.description: Segments the curve between U1 and U2 which can be out of the bounds of the curve. The curve is oriented from U1 to U2. The control points are modified, the first and the last point are not the same but the parametrization range is [0, 1] else it could not be a Bezier curve. Warnings: Even if <me> is not closed it can become closed after the segmentation for example if U1 or U2 are out of the bounds of the curve <me> or if the curve makes loop. After the segmentation the length of a curve can be null.

method.name: SetPole_1
method.description: Substitutes the pole of range index with P. If the curve <me> is rational the weight of range Index is not modified. raiseD if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles]

method.name: SetPole_2
method.description: Substitutes the pole and the weights of range Index. If the curve <me> is not rational it can become rational if all the weights are not identical. If the curve was rational it can become non rational if all the weights are identical. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles] Raised if Weight <= Resolution from package gp

method.name: SetWeight
method.description: Changes the weight of the pole of range Index. If the curve <me> is not rational it can become rational if all the weights are not identical. If the curve was rational it can become non rational if all the weights are identical. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles] Raised if Weight <= Resolution from package gp

method.name: IsClosed
method.description: Returns True if the distance between the first point and the last point of the curve is lower or equal to the Resolution from package gp.

method.name: IsCN
method.description: Continuity of the curve, returns True.

method.name: IsPeriodic
method.description: Returns False. A BezierCurve cannot be periodic in this package

method.name: IsRational
method.description: Returns false if all the weights are identical. The tolerance criterion is Resolution from package gp.

method.name: Continuity
method.description: Returns GeomAbs_CN, which is the continuity of any Bezier curve.

method.name: Degree
method.description: Returns the polynomial degree of the curve. It is the number of poles less one. In this package the Degree of a Bezier curve cannot be greater than "MaxDegree".

method.name: EvalDN
method.description: For this Bezier curve, computes - the point P of parameter U, or - the point P and one or more of the following values: - V1, the first derivative vector, - V2, the second derivative vector, - V3, the third derivative vector. Note: the parameter U can be outside the bounds of the curve. Raises RangeError if N < 1.

method.name: EndPoint
method.description: Returns the end point or start point of this Bezier curve.

method.name: FirstParameter
method.description: Returns the value of the first parameter of this Bezier curve. This is 0.0, which gives the start point of this Bezier curve.

method.name: LastParameter
method.description: Returns the value of the last parameter of this Bezier curve. This is 1.0, which gives the end point of this Bezier curve.

method.name: NbPoles
method.description: Returns the number of poles for this Bezier curve.

method.name: Pole
method.description: Returns the pole of range Index. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles]

method.name: Poles_2
method.description: Returns all the poles of the curve.

method.name: Poles_1
method.description: Returns all the poles of the curve.

method.name: StartPoint
method.description: Returns Value (U=1), it is the first control point of the curve.

method.name: Weight
method.description: Returns the weight of range Index. Raised if Index is not in the range [1, NbPoles]

method.name: Weights_2
method.description: Returns all the weights of the curve.

method.name: WeightsArray
method.description: Returns a const reference to the weights array. For rational curves: the internal owning weights array. For non-rational curves: a non-owning view of unit weights from BSplCLib. The array is always sized to match NbPoles().

method.name: Transform
method.description: Applies the transformation T to this Bezier curve.

method.name: Resolution
method.description: Computes for this Bezier curve the parametric tolerance UTolerance for a given tolerance Tolerance3D (relative to dimensions in the plane). If f(t) is the equation of this Bezier curve, UTolerance ensures that | t1 - t0| < Utolerance ===> |f(t1) - f(t0)| < ToleranceUV

method.name: Copy
method.description: Creates a new object which is a copy of this Bezier curve.

method.name: DumpJson
method.description: Dumps the content of me into the stream

method.name: Knots
method.description: Returns Bezier knots {0.0, 1.0} as a static array.

method.name: Multiplicities
method.description: Returns Bezier multiplicities for the current degree.

method.name: KnotSequence
method.description: Returns Bezier flat knots for the current degree.

method.name: MaxDegree
method.description: Returns the value of the maximum polynomial degree of a BezierCurve. This value is 25.
